title: Few-Shot Ordinal Learning for Day-Wise Freshness Estimation with Hyperspectral Fish Images
abstract: arXiv:2608.12230v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Non-destructive food quality assessment has increasingly benefited from hyperspectral imaging (HSI), which captures spectral signatures linked to biochemical changes during storage. Estimating day-wise freshness, however, remains challenging owing to strong inter-fillet variability and scarce labelled data per product. All existing deep learning approaches for HSI-based freshness prediction operate under full supervision, requiring densely annotated training sets that are costly to obtain at the individual-product level. We introduce, to the best of our knowledge, the first few-shot learning framework for HSI-based food quality estimation. Each fillet defines a distinct episodic task, and a CORAL-style ordinal prediction head captures the ranked nature of freshness progression through cumulative threshold modelling. translated_title: 少样本序数学习用于高光谱鱼肉图像的天级新鲜度估计
translated_abstract: 非破坏性食品质量评估日益受益于高光谱成像（HSI），该技术捕获储存过程中与生化变化相关的光谱特征。然而，由于鱼片间存在强烈变异性以及每个产品可用的标注数据稀缺，估计天级新鲜度仍然具有挑战性。所有现有的基于HSI的新鲜度预测深度学习方法都在全监督下运行，需要密集标注的训练集，这在单个产品层面获取成本高昂。我们首次引入了，据我们所知，基于HSI的食品质量估计的少样本学习框架。每个鱼片定义了一个独特的情节任务，一个CORAL风格的序数预测头通过累积阈值建模捕获新鲜度进展的排序性质。生物学的单调性和嵌入平滑性约束进一步引导预测朝着合理的轨迹发展。
tldr: 本文首次提出基于少样本学习的框架用于高光谱鱼肉图像的新鲜度估计，通过序数预测和生物约束实现无需密集标注的天级预测。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the first few-shot learning framework for hyperspectral fish image freshness estimation, using ordinal prediction with biological constraints to achieve day-wise prediction without dense annotations.
